feedback:
Tests: T3/T4 — High: Add regressions for changed configurations arriving through cache-bypassed request paths, failed replacement-watcher startup followed by another change, and an older request resuming client lookup after reload. The reference fails these scenarios despite passing the submitted tests.
T4 — High: Cover same-server credential changes and OIDC changes beyond ClientID, including request-supplied kubeconfigs. A deliberately incomplete implementation ignoring these changes passed all seven focused tests.
T3/T4 — Medium: The POST test checks watcher replacement but not clientset eviction. The scoped-eviction test checks only the remaining count, not which client survived. Assert the affected client changes and an unrelated client remains usable.
T1/T4 — Medium: The exact-name baseline filter silently omits suffixed tests and important existing clientset, middleware, and stateless regressions. Current baseline reports contain only 25 cases. Run the affected offline-compatible package suites or a verified complete selection.
T1/T6: Fix the ten pinned-linter findings in submitted tests and remove benchmark-purpose narration from the tests and harness.

Minor harness improvement: Report-generation errors are swallowed, and the fallback can write plain text to the XML path. Fix this, but it is not evidence of a current environment blocker: the downloaded runs contain genuine per-test JUnit reports.

Solution & Code: S1 — High: Bypassed requests leave the old watcher active. A request carrying an updated kubeconfig through /version reaches the new server and updates the stored context, but reconciliation is skipped. The old watcher remains active and no replacement starts. Reproduced on the reference and a passing agent.
S1 — High: Failed replacements break later eviction. Start watcher A, replace it with B whose discovery fails, then change to C. C’s watcher starts, but client lookup still contacts B because failed-watcher cleanup removed the configuration record used to detect changes. Reproduced three times.
S1 — High: Delayed old requests can repopulate stale clients. After reconciliation changes A to B, an older request can resume client lookup using A and cache that client under the current generation. A subsequent lookup using B then contacts A. Reproduced ten times using real HTTP servers and public client methods.
S2 — Medium: Generation metadata grows indefinitely for removed context keys. After 1,000 removals and expiry cleanup, client, in-flight, and blocked-prefix state were empty, but all 1,000 generation entries remained. Reclaim inactive metadata without allowing stale work to become current.
S2: Fix the two remaining pinned-linter findings in the reference’s watcher code and test adapter.

Other notes: Effective scope remains below the live minimum. The three passing implementations contain approximately 103, 106, and 237 effective production LOC, giving a median of 106, below the current 200-LOC requirement. Including testing-reset helpers still leaves the median at 110. Address this through substantive scope, not padding.

feedback:
Tests: T3/T4: Add regressions for the demonstrated failures:
- Missing-then-present context: initial reconciliation misses the context, but a later lookup finds it. Verify that this request cannot overwrite a replacement configuration’s cached response.
- Independent WebSocket resolution: resolve the same incoming request twice without modifying it. The existing middleware-chain test permits memoization to conceal destructive identity parsing.
- Cross-cluster isolation: hold one cached response’s writer open and verify that another cluster can still reconcile and serve requests.

T2/T3: Make the critical concurrency checks deterministic. The current-waiter test releases stale construction after 100 Gosched calls without confirming that the current caller reached the relevant boundary. The concurrent-request test similarly relies on repeated racing. Keep stress coverage, but add explicit synchronization proving the required interleavings. Stable repeated runs do not establish that these tests reliably catch incorrect implementations.

Solution & Code: S1 — Unstamped requests can repopulate stale responses. When reconciliation cannot find a context, downstream resolution can nevertheless find one and proceed without a configuration stamp. requestConfigurationIsCurrent treats that missing stamp as current. I reproduced an old-server request overwriting a newer server’s cached response, which a subsequent request then receives. Failed 10/10 repetitions. Preserve the failed resolution or reconcile the fallback before allowing configuration-sensitive caching.
S1 — WebSocket identity remains single-use outside the memoized chain. Resolution removes the identity subprotocol. Calling the exported resolver twice on the same unchanged WebSocket request succeeds first, then falls back to the shared key and fails lookup. Failed 10/10 repetitions. Preserve repeatable identity resolution and strip outbound-only metadata at the appropriate proxy boundary.
S2 — A slow cache reader blocks unrelated clusters. LoadFromCacheIfCurrent holds the global reconciliation mutex while writing the HTTP response. A blocked writer therefore prevents other clusters’ requests from reconciling or proceeding. This reproduces on both the reference and the passing agent; the pinned baseline passes the same probe. Keep blocking response I/O outside shared reconciliation locks.
S2: Fix the pinned golangci-lint v2.12.2 failures: 3 in the default affected-package run and 78 with reconciliation tests enabled. Findings span the implementation, test adapter, and submitted tests.
S4: Shorten the reference’s extensive explanatory blocks. Retain concise comments for genuinely non-obvious synchronization invariants.

Other notes: Resolved from v1: bypass reconciliation, failed-watcher configuration retention, the previously demonstrated stale-client poisoning, credential/OIDC coverage, POST/scoped-eviction assertions, baseline selection, and JUnit failure propagation.
Still unresolved: lint cleanliness and lengthy test/harness commentary explaining test purpose, implementation choices, and detection probability.

feedback:
Tests: T1 — Base mode fails offline as a non-root user. TestRenameCluster rewrites the checkout-owned headlamp_testdata/kubeconfig_rename fixture. Restore the temporary-copy fix that existed in v2.
T3/T4 — TestPassThroughRequestReloadsWatcher does not require the new watcher immediately after the pass-through request. It issues another cacheable request first. The nominally passing agent therefore stops A during the bypass but delays starting B until the later request, directly violating the prompt.
T3/T4 — Extend pass-through coverage beyond SelfSubjectAccessReview:
- A non-Kubernetes path such as /version.
- A WebSocket upgrade.
- Assert B’s watcher immediately after each bypass, before any normal request.
T3/T4 — Credential-only and OIDC-only cases merely inspect the stored context. They do not prove watcher replacement, clientset eviction, or response-cache eviction. An implementation performing full cleanup only for server changes passes.
T4 — OIDC coverage changes only client-id. Add another material setting such as issuer, secret, or scope.
T3/T4 — Add an unrelated-key control proving eviction is scoped. Globally clearing all response and client caches currently passes. Also retain a non-GET replacement case; every submitted request currently uses GET.
T2/T3 — Replace the stale-watcher Sleep/Never scheduling window with explicit synchronization proving the old cleanup has reached the contested registration step.
T1/T6 — test.sh resolves relative --output_path values after changing into backend, and it can return only the test status when report generation also fails. Shorten its extensive explanatory comment.

Solution & Code: S1 — An older request can resurrect the replaced watcher:
1. Request A captures configuration A and waits during authorization.
2. A pass-through request replaces it with B and starts B’s watcher.
3. B’s discovery fails, so B’s watcher unregisters.
4. A resumes and unconditionally calls CheckForChanges with its captured configuration.
5. Because the registry is now empty, watcher A is registered again even though the store still contains B.
The current configuration check protects response and clientset caching, but not this post-authorization watcher start. Validate ownership/current generation before registration.
S4 — Trim the remaining tutorial-style synchronization commentary, especially in the harness.

Other notes: Resolved: missing-context stale response writes, the global lock around response-writer I/O, formatting failures, and most excessive commentary.
Superseded: the earlier independent WebSocket-resolution requirement was removed from the revised contract.
Regressed: non-root baseline compatibility, POST coverage, scoped-eviction controls, and complete credential/OIDC lifecycle assertions.

Reference has 187 LOC
